text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- Railway strike continues for the 11th day on Friday as the government refused to increase railway salaries.
- The NATO council said it has not yet decided whether Slovenia will be included in the first round of NATO expansion.
- The parliament elected Eda Okretic-Salmic, a member of the pensioners' party Desus, as deputy president of the assembly.
- The Ljubljana city council still has to determine the city's 1997 budget.
- The parliament elected Marjan Schiffrer, a member of the Christian Democrats, as head of a parliamentary board for contact with Slovenians who live abroad.
- Bank SKB said it would buy 51 percent of bank UBK in order to form a new banking group.
- Lawyers have said it would be too expensive to build a new Ljubljana court and suggested the court buys additional space in the centre of Ljubljana.
- National television RTV Slovenia said it would start to broadcast satellite radio and television programmes in the autumn.
- According to the Finance Ministry the number of people in government employment rose by 485 to 32,202 from January to the end of April.
